newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends down on speculative selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends down on speculative selling.

text.p: Shanghai Soybean futures ended mostly down on Wednesday on speculative selling, traders said.
The most active November 1997 contract ended at 3,310 yuan ($399) per tonne, losing 15 yuan. It opened at 3,300 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 3,296 and a high of 3,330.
July rose five yuan to 3,255, September fell eight yuan to 3,310, the January 1998 contract fell 100 to 3,172 and March lost 120 to 3,210.
Combined volume rose to 17,600 tonnes from 15,900.
Soybean opened lower and fell further due to speculative selling from retail investors, traders said.
"Under the pressure of speculative selling and with few investors building new positions, late-maturing contracts fell sharply, depressing the early-maturing contracts as well," one trader said.
"But strong physical prices supported the early-maturing contracts to some extent, preventing them from falling sharply," he added.
Physical prices are around 3,300 yuan in the Shanghai area.
Traders expected the early-maturing contracts to move around the current level in the short term.
